transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

My head keeps getting stuck on these awful what‑if scenarios about things going wrong with the wiring, and I can’t shut the thoughts off long enough to do my job. It's just become completely overwhelming lately and I don't know how to make it stop.
Do these distressing thoughts lead you to do certain actions or mental rituals to reduce the anxiety, like checking things repeatedly or counting in your head?

Yes, to calm down I end up going back to the same outlet or panel five or ten times—flipping breakers, tugging on wires, and re-reading the code book under my breath. I have to do it until I feel this physical 'click' in my chest that tells me it's safe. If it doesn't feel just right, I have to restart the whole thing from the beginning, even if it makes me late or forces me to walk away from the job entirely.
Do these thoughts and checking rituals happen every day, and how much time do they usually take up in your day?

Yes, it's a daily struggle that is completely taking over my life, especially when I'm trying to work or when I'm alone in my apartment at night. I waste hours checking the same outlet five to ten times, which makes me incredibly late, prevents me from finishing walkthroughs, and has ultimately cost me major jobs and all my free time.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was [F42], and based on this conversation, F42 remains the most consistent diagnosis. The patient describes recurrent, intrusive thoughts about electrical safety (obsessions) and repetitive checking behaviors (compulsions) that are time-consuming, cause significant distress, and impair occupational functioning. The need to repeat actions until a 'just right' feeling occurs and the associated mental rituals align strongly with the diagnostic criteria for obsessive-compulsive disorder. No new symptoms suggesting alternative diagnoses (e.g., mood disorders, psychosis, or anxiety disorders without compulsivity) have emerged.
